## Wikipedia Citation Opportunity Engine
Detects explicit Wikipedia citation gaps and converts them into clear, structured content opportunities aligned to a user page.

parameters.text:
=## Context

You are evaluating whether a Wikipedia article provides a direct conceptual explanation of a specific term associated with a user page’s topic domain.

The term and its reason explain how the concept is used by the user page. The Wikipedia page markdown represents the actual scope and focus of the article.

This evaluation is used to decide whether the Wikipedia page is worth deeper analysis for citation opportunity discovery. The goal is to score conceptual relevance and explanatory proximity, not authority, completeness, or citation quality.

⸻

## Instructions
1.  Use ONLY the provided inputs:
•	term: a domain-defining term representing the user page’s topic area
•	reason: a short explanation of why this term belongs to the user page’s topic domain
•	wiki_title: title of the Wikipedia article
•	wiki_snippet: short excerpt returned by Wikipedia search
•	wiki_page_markdown: full markdown content of the Wikipedia article
2.  Understand the user page’s topic domain
•	Treat "term" as the authoritative representation of the user page’s subject area
•	Use "reason" to understand how the term is used and interpreted on the user page
•	Do NOT require Wikipedia wording to match the reason
•	Do NOT infer scope beyond this term
3.  Evaluate Wikipedia page relevance
•	Assess whether the Wikipedia article primarily explains the term itself
•	Determine whether the term is:
    •	a central subject of the article, or
    •	only mentioned incidentally within a broader topic
•	Prefer Wikipedia pages that:
    •	define, explain, or contextualise the term as a standalone concept
    •	would naturally be cited when explaining the term
•	Penalise pages that:
    •	represent broader umbrella categories. But do NOT penalise scoped Wikipedia articles when the term itself is scoped
    •	focus mainly on parent concepts, asset classes, or domains
    •	only mention the term briefly or peripherally
    •	if the Wikipedia article could not reasonably be used to define or explain the term in a reference-style sentence
•	Scoring Guidelines:
    •	90–100 → Canonical article directly explaining the term
    •	70–89 → Strong relevance; term is a major subtopic
    •	50–69 → Partial or ambiguous relevance
    •	<50 → Weak or unsuitable match
•   Apply generic-term and scoped-term intent rules:
    •   If the term is broad, generic, or category-level
        •   Strongly prefer Wikipedia articles that explain the general concept itself
        •   Penalise pages that represent: specific government programs, temporary schemes, jurisdiction-specific initiatives, named policies or acts   
    •   If the term includes explicit scope indicators, such as country, jurisdiction, legal act, policy reference, or time-bound or named initiatives
        •   Strongly prefer Wikipedia articles that match the same scope exactly
        •   Generic umbrella pages MUST be penalised if they do not reflect the same scope
    •	Apply specificity preference
        •	If multiple pages are relevant, the page most specific to the term must score higher
        •	Broader parent concepts must not outrank direct explanatory pages
4.  Apply strict constraints
•	Base judgment on wiki_title, wiki_snippet, and wiki_page_markdown only
•	Do NOT assume additional content
•	Do NOT hallucinate details
•	If relevance is unclear, score conservatively
•	relevance_score must be an integer between 0 and 100
•	Do not return decimal values
•	wiki_title in the output must exactly match the input wiki_title

⸻

## Task
Return ONLY valid JSON in the exact structure shown below.
{
  "wiki_title": "Home insurance",
  "relevance_score": 80,
  "score_reason": "The article directly explains home insurance as a standalone concept and covers its scope and purpose, making it suitable as a primary explanatory reference for the term."
}

⸻

## Inputs to Consider
term: {{ $('Loop Over Items2').item.json.term }}
reason: {{ $('Loop Over Items2').item.json.reason }}
wiki_title: {{ $json.wiki_title }}
wiki_snippet: {{ $json.wiki_snippet }}
wiki_page_markdown: {{ $json.wiki_page_markdown }}

parameters.text:
=## Context

You are an AI assistant responsible only for generating content suggestions for a user page, based on Wikipedia citation gaps that have already been identified by a previous process.

The Wikipedia citation gap has already been:
•	correctly detected,
•	correctly classified (inline, section, or article),
•	correctly extracted as an exact snippet.

You must not analyze Wikipedia, re-classify gaps, or question the extraction.

Your role is purely generative: suggest neutral, reference-style content that the user page could publish to help support the specific citation gap provided.

This task is strictly about content suggestion, not discovery or validation.

⸻

## Instructions
1.  Use ONLY the provided inputs:
•	term: the specific concept associated with the user page
•	reason: explanation of how the term relates to the user page
•	user_page_markdown: full markdown content from the user page. This represents existing content and MUST be considered when suggesting additions or improvements.
•	wiki_title: title of the Wikipedia article
•	wikipedia_opportunity_type: classification of the snippet opportunity type, one of: inline, section, or article
•	wikipedia_opportunity_snippet: the exact text extracted from Wikipedia that is explicitly marked as needing citations
•	Scope boundaries (strict):
    •	Do NOT analyze Wikipedia beyond the provided snippet
    •	Do NOT infer additional citation gaps
    •	Do NOT validate factual accuracy
    •	Do NOT invent claims, data, or sources
    •	Do NOT use external knowledge
2.  Interpret opportunity type correctly
•	Your content suggestion MUST align with wikipedia_opportunity_type:
    •	Inline:
        •	Represents a single statement or sentence
        •   Suggest focused, narrowly scoped content
        •   Typically one subsection, explainer, or clarification
    •	Section:
        •   Represents an entire section lacking citations
        •   Suggest structured, multi-point content
        •   Appropriate for step-by-step or process explanations
    •	Article:
        •   Represents an article-wide citation banner
        •   Suggest foundational, high-level reference content
        •   Do NOT attempt to cover every claim in the article
3.  Use the user page as the anchor
    •	Review user_page_markdown before suggesting content
    •	Avoid duplicating existing explanations
    •	Prefer:
        •   expansions,
        •   clarifications,
        •   structured additions,
        •   missing conceptual coverage
4.  Generate a content suggestion
•	For each wikipedia_opportunity_snippet, provide a clear content brief structured as:
    •	what_to_publish: A plain-language description of the content the user should create or expand
    •	suggested_page_focus: The scope, angle, or framing the content should take
    •	content_outline: Bullet points describing the key sections or points to cover
    •	how_this_supports_wikipedia: A short explanation of how this content supports the specific Wikipedia citation gap / opportunity snippet
•	Tone & constraints
    •	Neutral, reference-style tone
    •	Explain what content should be published
    •	No promotional language
    •	No speculative or unverifiable claims
•	Special handling for article-level citation signals:
    •	Provide one general content brief only
    •	Focus on foundational, high-level explanatory content
    •	Do NOT attempt to address every article claim

⸻

## Task
Return ONLY valid JSON in the exact structure shown below.
Do NOT add extra keys.
Do NOT include explanations outside JSON.
{
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "wiki_title": "Home insurance",
      "term": "home insurance",
      "wikipedia_opportunity_type": "inline",
      "wikipedia_opportunity_snippet": "Home insurance policies typically cover damage caused by fire, theft, and certain natural disasters, although the specific coverage varies by policy and jurisdiction. [citation needed]",
      "user_page_content_suggestion": {
        "what_to_publish": "A neutral explainer describing the types of coverage commonly included in home insurance policies.",
        "suggested_page_focus": "Standard perils, exclusions, and how coverage varies by policy and jurisdiction.",
        "content_outline": [
          "Purpose and definition of home insurance",
          "Common perils typically covered",
          "Jurisdictional and policy-based variations",
          "Typical exclusions and limitations"
        ],
        "how_this_supports_wikipedia": "This content directly supports a statement that is explicitly marked as needing a citation."
      }
    }
  ]
}

⸻

## Inputs to Consider
term: {{ $json.term }}
reason: {{ $json.reason }}
user_page_markdown: {{ $json.user_page_markdown }}
wiki_title: {{ $json.wiki_title }}
wikipedia_opportunity_type: {{ $json.wikipedia_opportunity_type }}
wikipedia_opportunity_snippet: {{ $json.wikipedia_opportunity_snippet }}

parameters.text:
=## Context

You are analysing the markdown content of a web page.

The page represents a product, service, or informational offering and is used to determine the topic domain the site operates in.

This analysis is to identify neutral concepts, entities, and terminology associated with this topic in educational or reference-style explanations.

The output will be used as a topic anchor for downstream relevance evaluation and citation opportunity discovery.

⸻

## Instructions
1.  Use ONLY the provided inputs:
•	user_page_markdown: cleaned markdown extracted from the user-provided URL
•	user_page_primary_content: suggested primary content context for the page
2.  Determine the page’s authority scope
•	Identify what the page is about in neutral, encyclopedic terms
•	Base conclusions primarily on the page markdown
•	Use user_page_primary_content only as supporting context
•	Do not infer authority beyond what the content supports
3.  Extract relevant terms and concepts
•	Identify terms someone would reasonably expect when explaining this topic in an educational or reference context
•	Include:
    •	synonyms and alternative phrasings
    •	related entities, concepts, processes, and definitions
    •	industry-standard terminology
•	Exclude:
    •	marketing slogans
    •	brand or product names (unless essential proper nouns)
    •	calls to action, pricing, testimonials
    •	navigation or boilerplate text
4.  Provide a short reason for each term
•	For each term, explain why it belongs to the page’s topic domain
•	The reason should:
    •	be 1–2 sentences maximum
    •	describe how the term relates to the page content
    •	be explanatory, not definitional
    •	avoid restating the term verbatim
•	Do not use promotional or persuasive language
5.  Normalise and deduplicate
•	Merge near-duplicates (singular/plural, phrasing variants)
•	Prefer canonical, widely accepted terminology
•	Avoid overly generic terms (e.g. “solution”, “service”, “benefits”)
6.  Apply output constraints
•	Extract between 5 and 10 high-signal terms
•	Each term must be specific and meaningful for downstream matching
•	Use lowercase unless the term is a proper noun

⸻

## Task
Return ONLY valid JSON in the exact structure shown below.
Do NOT add extra keys.
Do NOT include explanations outside JSON.
{
  "terms": [
    {
      "term": "commercial real estate loans",
      "reason": "The page discusses financing structures used to acquire or refinance income-producing properties."
    },
    {
      "term": "rent reviews",
      "reason": "The page references mechanisms for adjusting rental income over time, which impacts valuation and cash flow."
    }
  ]
}

⸻

## Inputs to Consider
user_page_markdown: {{ $json.user_page_markdown }}
user_page_primary_content: {{ $json.user_page_primary_content }}

## 3. Identify Top Matching Wikipedia Page
Finds, evaluates, and selects the most conceptually relevant Wikipedia page for citation analysis.

## 4. Detect Citation Gaps
Scans the selected Wikipedia page to detect explicitly marked citation gaps by type.

parameters.text:
=## Context

You are analyzing a Wikipedia article to extract explicitly marked citation gaps.

Your goal is to:
•	identifying citation gap types
•	extracting the exact snippet from the provided Wikipedia markdown

You must NOT generate explanations, summaries, or suggested content.

This is a deterministic extraction task.

⸻

## Instructions
1.  Use ONLY the provided inputs:
•	wiki_page_markdown: full markdown content of the Wikipedia article.
•	Do NOT use external knowledge.
•	Do NOT invent text.
2.  Identify explicit Wikipedia citation signals
•	You MUST treat citation gaps as purely text-based signals AND position-based signals.
•	You MUST treat a citation gap as INLINE notices only if:
    •	The exact phrase "citation needed", "additional citation needed", or "better source needed" appear in `wiki_page_markdown`.
    •	Appears INLINE within a sentence
•	If none of the above phrases appear, no citation gap exists.
3.  Extraction rules (STRICT)
•	For EACH detected citation signal:
    •	Extract a continuous text span ending at the inline citation notice (including inline marker [] if any). The extracted span MUST be grammatically complete, semantically self-contained and understandable.
    •	Assign the opportunity as: wikipedia_opportunity_type = "inline"
    •	Do NOT include more text than necessary.
    •	Do NOT include headings, other paragraphs, or lists.
4.  Hard constraints (MANDATORY)
•   Every extracted snippet MUST exist verbatim in `wiki_page_markdown`
•	Do NOT merge multiple citation gaps
•	Do NOT rewrite, paraphrase, or normalize text

⸻

## Task
Return ONLY valid JSON in the exact structure shown below.
Do NOT add extra keys.
Do NOT include explanations outside JSON.
{
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "wikipedia_opportunity_type": "inline",
      "wikipedia_opportunity_snippet": "The amount of insurance contribution is determined by several criteria, like the region, the type of car or the personal way of driving. [citation needed]"
    }
  ]
}

⸻

## Inputs to Consider
wiki_page_markdown: {{ $('Set Wiki Page Content').item.json.wiki_page_markdown }}

=## Context

You are analyzing a Wikipedia article to extract explicitly marked citation gaps.

Your goal is to:
•	identifying citation gap types
•	extracting the exact snippet from the provided Wikipedia markdown

You must NOT generate explanations, summaries, or suggested content.

This is a deterministic extraction task.

⸻

## Instructions
1.  Use ONLY the provided inputs:
•	wiki_page_markdown: full markdown content of the Wikipedia article.
•	Do NOT use external knowledge.
•	Do NOT invent text.
2.  Identify explicit Wikipedia citation signals
•	You MUST treat citation gaps as purely text-based signals.
•	You MUST identify a citation gap whenever ANY of the following exact phrases appear anywhere in `wiki_page_markdown`:
    A.	Section-level notices:
        •   This section does not cite any sources
        •   This section needs additional citations
        •   Whenever any of the above phrases appear, classify the opportunity as: wikipedia_opportunity_type = "section" 
    B.	Article-level notices:
        •   Any banner or notice clearly stating that the article requires additional citations
        •   Classify these as: wikipedia_opportunity_type = "article"
•	If none of the above phrases appear, you MUST assume no citation gap exists.
3.  Extraction rules (STRICT)
•	For EACH detected citation signal:
    •	Assign `wikipedia_opportunity_type` as one of:
        •	section
        •	article
    •	Extract the snippet EXACTLY as it appears in `wiki_page_markdown`.
    •	Extraction behavior by type:
        A.  SECTION
            •	Extract the section heading (if present), the citation notice text, and the immediately following section content.
            •	Stop at the next major heading.
        B.  ARTICLE
            •	Extract ONLY the article-level citation notice text.
            •	Do NOT extract article body content.
4.  Hard constraints (MANDATORY)
•   Every extracted snippet MUST exist verbatim in `wiki_page_markdown`
•	Do NOT merge multiple citation gaps
•	Do NOT rewrite, paraphrase, or normalize text

⸻

## Task
Return ONLY valid JSON in the exact structure shown below.
Do NOT add extra keys.
Do NOT include explanations outside JSON.
{
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "wikipedia_opportunity_type": "section",
      "wikipedia_opportunity_snippet": "Germany\nThis section does not cite any sources. Please help improve this section by adding citations to reliable sources.\n\nSince 1939, it has been compulsory to have third-party personal insurance before keeping a motor vehicle in all federal states of Germany. In addition, every vehicle owner is free to take out a comprehensive insurance policy."
    },
    {
      "wikipedia_opportunity_type": "article",
      "wikipedia_opportunity_snippet": "This article needs additional citations for verification. Please help improve this article by adding citations to reliable sources. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed."
    }
  ]
}

⸻

## Inputs to Consider
wiki_page_markdown: {{ $('Set Wiki Page Content').item.json.wiki_page_markdown }}
